item.title: What's happening with the American takeover of Sweden's Northvolt?
item.description: In March 2025 Swedish electric battery manufacturer Northvolt became the largest bankruptcy case in modern Swedish history. An American company called Lyten has now finalized its purchase of Northvolt's assets and is rehiring in Sweden.

item.title: American company Lyten completes purchase of Sweden's Northvolt
item.description: Lyten, an American lithium-sulphur battery and energy storage company, announced today that it has completed its purchase of the former Northvolt factories in Skellefteå and Northvolt Labs in Västerås. The deal is valued at 45 billion kronor.

item.title: Ombudsman to re-investigate waiting times at Swedish Migration Agency
item.description: Sweden's Parliamentary Ombudsman (JO) Per Lennerbrant has agreed to carry out yet another investigation of long waiting times at the Migration Agency as the average wait for citizenship hits 47 months.

item.title: TELL US: Which are the best districts for foreigners in Gothenburg?
item.description: From Majorna, with its cafés and boutiques, to suburbs like Eriksberg, Kålltorp and Mölndal, people living in Gothenburg are spoiled for choice. We want to hear from readers about which district is best for foreigners.

item.title: Politics in Sweden: Will there still be a left-wing and right-wing bloc come September?
item.description: One party looks likely to drop out of parliament at the next election and there are splits in both the governing and opposition blocs on key issues. But will the current blocs even exist in the same form after the election?

item.description: Have you been paying attention to the headlines? Do Saturday morning fika right with a cup of coffee and a mental workout. Every Saturday morning, we bring you a fresh crossword and word search that test your grasp of the Swedish zeitgeist.

item.title: OPINION: 'Sweden's parliament should add transitional rules to the citizenship law'
item.description: If Sweden’s parliament passes a new citizenship law without transitional rules, it risks undermining the reputation for fairness and stability that has long helped Sweden attract skilled international workers, says Patrick Gallen, spokesperson of the Fair Transition campaign.

item.title: How to influence political decisions on Sweden's new citizenship rules
item.description: A number of The Local's readers have reached out since more details of the planned changes to Swedish citizenship rules were unveiled in February asking how they can share their opinions with decision-makers. Here are a few ways to do so.
